facts.name: Contingent Beneficiary Designation
facts.sentence: The contingent beneficiary is the estate of Theodora M. Anagnos.

facts.name: Statutory Authority Basis
facts.sentence: This life insurance plan was established pursuant to Cascade State Code §44-7200 et seq.

facts.name: Public Employee Benefits Act
facts.sentence: Cascade State Code §44-7200 et seq. is known as the Public Employee Benefits Act.

facts.name: Plan Administration Authority
facts.sentence: The Department of Administration, Office of Employee Benefits administers this plan.

facts.name: Administrative Oversight by OEB
facts.sentence: The administrative office responsible for managing the plan is called OEB.

facts.name: Master Group Policy Coverage
facts.sentence: Coverage under this plan is provided through a master group policy.

facts.name: Master Policy Issuer
facts.sentence: The master group policy is issued by Pacific Trust Life & Annuity.

facts.name: Master Policy Issuance
facts.sentence: Pacific Trust Life & Annuity issues the master group policy to the State of Cascade.

facts.name: Legal Precedence Clause
facts.sentence: In case of conflict between this certificate and applicable law, Cascade state law prevails.

facts.name: Master Policy Supremacy
facts.sentence: In case of conflict between this certificate and the master policy, the master policy prevails.

facts.name: ERISA Exemption Status
facts.sentence: This plan is exempt from ERISA regulations.

facts.name: ERISA Exemption Basis
facts.sentence: The exemption from ERISA applies because this is a governmental plan.

facts.name: ERISA Exemption Basis
facts.sentence: ERISA §4(b)(1) establishes the exemption for governmental plans.

facts.name: Employee Coverage Choice
facts.sentence: Eligible state employees may choose from the available coverage options listed in Section 2.

facts.name: Basic Life Eligibility
facts.sentence: Option A (Basic Life) is available to eligible state employees.

facts.name: Basic Life Coverage Amount
facts.sentence: Option A (Basic Life) offers coverage equal to 1 times the employee’s salary.

facts.name: Basic Life Coverage Amount
facts.sentence: Option A (Basic Life) provides coverage equal to 1x annual base salary.

facts.name: Basic Life Availability
facts.sentence: Option A (Basic Life) is available to all eligible employees.

facts.name: Employer Subsidy for Basic Life
facts.sentence: The employer subsidizes 60% of the premium for Option A (Basic Life).

facts.name: Automatic Enrollment
facts.sentence: Enrollment in Option A (Basic Life) is automatic.

facts.name: Written Waiver Required
facts.sentence: Declining Option A (Basic Life) requires a written waiver.

facts.name: 2x Basic Life Coverage
facts.sentence: Option B (2x Basic Life) provides coverage equal to 2x annual base salary.

facts.name: Employer Subsidy for Option B
facts.sentence: The employer subsidizes 60% of the premium for Option B (2x Basic Life).

facts.name: Option B EOI Requirement
facts.sentence: Election of Option B (2x Basic Life) requires Evidence of Insurability (EOI) unless elected within 31 days of initial eligibility.

facts.name: Additional 1x Optional Life Coverage
facts.sentence: Option C (Optional Life – 1x) provides additional coverage equal to 1x annual base salary on top of Option A.

facts.name: Employee-Paid Optional Life
facts.sentence: Option C (Optional Life – 1x) is paid entirely by the employee.

facts.name: Option C EOI Waiver Window
facts.sentence: No EOI is required for Option C (Optional Life – 1x) if elected within 31 days of initial eligibility.

facts.name: EOI Requirement for Late Option C Election
facts.sentence: EOI is required for Option C (Optional Life – 1x) if elected more than 31 days after initial eligibility.

facts.name: Additional 2x Optional Life Coverage
facts.sentence: Option D (Optional Life – 2x) provides additional coverage equal to 2x annual base salary on top of Option A.

facts.name: Employee-Paid Optional Life
facts.sentence: Option D (Optional Life – 2x) is paid entirely by the employee.

facts.name: Option D EOI Requirement
facts.sentence: EOI is required for Option D (Optional Life – 2x) at all times.

facts.name: Permanent Classified Eligibility
facts.sentence: Eligibility for life insurance coverage extends to all permanent classified civil service employees.

facts.name: Permanent Unclassified Eligibility
facts.sentence: Eligibility for life insurance coverage extends to all permanent unclassified civil service employees.

facts.name: Full-Time Employee Eligibility
facts.sentence: Eligibility for life insurance coverage includes full-time employees.

facts.name: Part-Time Eligibility
facts.sentence: Eligibility for life insurance coverage includes part-time employees who work between 50% and 99% of full-time equivalent hours.

facts.name: Pro-Rated Part-Time Coverage
facts.sentence: Part-time employees receive benefits on a pro-rated basis based on their percentage of full-time equivalent employment.

facts.name: Temporary Employee Exclusion
facts.sentence: Temporary employees are not eligible for life insurance coverage.

facts.name: Contract Employee Ineligibility
facts.sentence: Contract employees are not eligible for life insurance coverage.

facts.name: Contractor Ineligibility
facts.sentence: Contractors employed through third-party staffing agencies are not eligible for life insurance coverage.

facts.name: Open Enrollment Timing
facts.sentence: Annual open enrollment occurs in November.

facts.name: Open Enrollment Changes Without EOI
facts.sentence: Employees may change coverage options during the 15-day open enrollment window without requiring Evidence of Insurability (EOI).

facts.name: EOI Required for Outside Open Enrollment Increases
facts.sentence: Option increases require Evidence of Insurability (EOI) when made outside the 15-day open enrollment window.

facts.name: Salary Basis for Benefit Calculation
facts.sentence: Annual base salary used for benefit calculation is as recorded on the certified payroll as of January 1.

facts.name: Salary Rounding Rule
facts.sentence: Annual base salary is rounded to the nearest $1,000 for benefit purposes.

facts.name: Annual Benefit Update Post-COLA
facts.sentence: Benefits are updated annually on January 1 following any salary change due to cost-of-living adjustments.

facts.name: Promotion-Based Benefit Update
facts.sentence: Benefits are updated annually on January 1 following any promotion.

facts.name: Benefit Update After Reclassification
facts.sentence: Benefits are updated annually on January 1 following any reclassification.

facts.name: Mid-Year Salary Change Rule
facts.sentence: Mid-year salary changes other than reclassification to a higher grade do not affect coverage until the next January 1 renewal.

facts.name: Age 65 Benefit Reduction
facts.sentence: At age 65, the life insurance benefit is reduced to 65% of the benefit in force at age 65.

facts.name: Age 70 Benefit Reduction
facts.sentence: At age 70, the life insurance benefit is reduced to 50% of the benefit in force.

facts.name: Age 65 Benefit Reduction
facts.sentence: Age 65 triggers a reduction to 65% of the benefit in force at age 65.

facts.name: Age 70 Benefit Reduction
facts.sentence: Age 70 triggers a reduction to 50% of the benefit in force at age 65.

facts.name: Equal Benefit Reduction Across Options
facts.sentence: The reduction applies equally to Options A, B, C, and D.

facts.name: Maximum Coverage Limit
facts.sentence: No single employee may have total coverage exceeding $600,000.

facts.name: CPEBCA Coverage Continuation
facts.sentence: Under the Cascade Public Employee Benefits Continuation Act (CPEBCA), employees who terminate employment may continue life coverage for up to 18 months.

facts.name: Payment Requirement for Continuation
facts.sentence: Continuation coverage requires payment of 100% of the group premium directly to OEB.

facts.name: Eligible Qualifying Event
facts.sentence: Voluntary resignation is an eligible qualifying event for continuation coverage.

facts.name: Eligible Termination Event
facts.sentence: Termination other than for gross misconduct is an eligible qualifying event for continuation coverage.

facts.name: Eligible Event: Reduced Hours
facts.sentence: Reduction in hours below the eligibility threshold is an eligible qualifying event for continuation coverage.

facts.name: Eligible Leave Event
facts.sentence: Approved leave of absence without pay beyond 12 weeks is an eligible qualifying event for continuation coverage.

facts.name: Continuation Coverage Scope
facts.sentence: Continuation coverage applies to Options A and C.

facts.name: Option B Continuation Election
facts.sentence: Option B coverage may be continued at the employee's election during the continuation period.

facts.name: Option D Continuation Election
facts.sentence: Option D coverage may be continued at the employee's election during the continuation period.

facts.name: CPEBCA vs Conversion Right
facts.sentence: CPEBCA continuation is separate from and in addition to any conversion right described in Section 5.

facts.name: Conversion Right After Termination
facts.sentence: Upon termination of group coverage for any reason except nonpayment of premium, the employee may convert to an individual whole-life policy.

facts.name: 31-Day Conversion Window
facts.sentence: Conversion to an individual whole-life policy must occur within 31 days of termination.

facts.name: No EOI for Conversion
facts.sentence: Conversion does not require evidence of insurability (EOI).

facts.name: Conversion Limit Cap
facts.sentence: Maximum convertible amount is the lesser of the coverage in force or $250,000.

facts.name: Conversion Timing Post-Continuation
facts.sentence: The conversion right may be exercised at the end of any CPEBCA continuation period.

facts.name: Conversion Window Start Date
facts.sentence: The 31-day window for exercising the conversion right begins on the date that continuation coverage ends.

facts.name: Retiree Coverage Eligibility
facts.sentence: Employees who retire through the State of Cascade Retirement System (SCRS) are eligible for retiree group term coverage.

facts.name: Retirement Service Requirement
facts.sentence: An employee must have at least 10 years of state service to qualify for retiree group term coverage under SCRS.

facts.name: Retirement Benefit Tier: 10–19 Years
facts.sentence: Retirees with 10–19 years of service at retirement receive a flat benefit of $15,000.

facts.name: Flat Benefit for 20–29 Years Service
facts.sentence: Retirees with 20–29 years of service at retirement receive a flat benefit of $25,000.

facts.name: $35K Benefit for 30+ Years Service
facts.sentence: Retirees with 30 or more years of service at retirement receive a flat benefit of $35,000.

facts.name: Employer-Funded Retiree Coverage
facts.sentence: Retiree coverage is funded entirely by the employer.

facts.name: Retiree Coverage Premium-Free
facts.sentence: No premium is charged to retirees for their group term coverage.

facts.name: Termination of Optional Life Coverage
facts.sentence: Optional life coverage options C and D terminate upon retirement.

facts.name: Optional Coverage Conversion Window
facts.sentence: Retirees may convert optional life coverage within 31 days of retirement.

facts.name: No Age Reduction Post-Retirement
facts.sentence: Once retiree status begins, retiree coverage is not subject to further age-based reductions.

facts.name: Terminal Illness Acceleration Eligibility
facts.sentence: Active employees and retirees diagnosed with a certified terminal illness may accelerate up to 50% of their total group life benefit.

facts.name: Maximum Acceleration Limit
facts.sentence: The maximum amount that may be accelerated due to terminal illness is $100,000.

facts.name: Minimum Acceleration Amount
facts.sentence: The minimum amount that may be accelerated due to terminal illness is $5,000.

facts.name: Actuarial Discount on Acceleration
facts.sentence: An actuarial discount applies to any accelerated death benefit payout.

facts.name: Accelerated Coverage Requirement
facts.sentence: For active employees, accelerating optional coverage requires also accelerating a proportional amount of basic coverage.

facts.name: Suicide Exclusion After 12 Months
facts.sentence: A suicide exclusion cannot be applied after 12 months of coverage under Cascade §44-7228.

facts.name: Suicide Benefit Exclusion (First Year)
facts.sentence: During the first 12 months of coverage, no basic or optional benefit is payable for death by suicide.

facts.name: Incontestability Clause After Two Years
facts.sentence: After two years of coverage, Pacific Trust may not deny a claim based on misrepresentation unless there was fraudulent intent to obtain coverage.

facts.name: No Pre-Existing Condition Exclusion
facts.sentence: There is no pre-existing condition exclusion in the policy.

facts.name: No Occupational Hazard Exclusion
facts.sentence: There is no exclusion for occupational hazards related to public safety duties.

facts.name: Equal Coverage for First Responders
facts.sentence: Law enforcement and firefighting personnel are covered under the same provisions as other employees.

facts.name: No Pre-Existing Condition Exclusion
facts.sentence: No pre-existing condition exclusion applies.

facts.name: No Exclusion for Public Safety Hazards
facts.sentence: There is no exclusion for occupational hazards related to public safety duties.

facts.name: No Exclusion for Line-of-Duty Death
facts.sentence: For employees in hazardous duty classifications such as firefighter, law enforcement, or corrections, no additional exclusion applies for death in the line of duty.
chunk_topics: death in the line of duty

facts.name: Automatic Premium Waiver
facts.sentence: Upon approval of a long-term disability claim under the State's Long-Term Disability plan (Plan 44-LTD), life insurance premiums are automatically waived.

facts.name: Automatic Premium Waiver
facts.sentence: A separate application is not required to waive life insurance premiums upon approval of a long-term disability claim.

facts.name: Premium Waiver Continuity During LTD
facts.sentence: Waiver of life insurance premiums continues while Long-Term Disability (LTD) benefits are payable.

facts.name: Benefit Level Stability During Waiver
facts.sentence: Coverage remains at the benefit level in force at the onset of disability during the waiver period.

facts.name: Waiver Benefit Stability
facts.sentence: The benefit level during the waiver period is not subject to annual salary recalculations.

facts.name: Premium Waiver Termination
facts.sentence: The waiver of premiums terminates when Long-Term Disability benefits end.

facts.name: Premium Waiver Termination
facts.sentence: The waiver of premiums terminates when the employee returns to active service.

facts.name: Premium Waiver Termination upon Retirement
facts.sentence: The waiver of premiums terminates when the employee retires.

facts.name: Premium Waiver Termination Age
facts.sentence: The waiver of premiums terminates when the employee attains age 70.

facts.name: Beneficiary Portal Management
facts.sentence: Beneficiary designations are maintained in the state's HR/Benefits portal.

facts.name: Beneficiary Update Process
facts.sentence: Beneficiary designations are updated through the employee's agency's HR representative.

facts.name: Minor Beneficiary Payment Rule
facts.sentence: If the designated beneficiary is a minor, benefits are paid to the court-appointed guardian of the minor's estate.

facts.name: Minor Beneficiary Payment Rule
facts.sentence: Benefits are paid to the court-appointed guardian of the minor's estate unless a trust has been designated.

facts.name: Beneficiary Claim Filing途径
facts.sentence: Claims may be filed by the beneficiary directly through OEB.

facts.name: Beneficiary Claim Filing Process
facts.sentence: Claims may be filed by the beneficiary directly through Pacific Trust.

facts.name: Claim Submission Address
facts.sentence: Claims should be submitted to Pacific Trust Life & Annuity – Public Sector Claims.

facts.name: Claim Submission Address
facts.sentence: Pacific Trust Life & Annuity – Public Sector Claims is located at 1000 Government Center Blvd., Capital City, CA 95814.

facts.name: Pacific Trust Contact Number
facts.sentence: The phone number for Pacific Trust Life & Annuity – Public Sector Claims is 1-888-555-6600.

facts.name: Claim Submission Portal Access
facts.sentence: State employees can submit claims via the state employee portal at benefits.cascade.gov/claims.

facts.name: Claim Processing Deadline
facts.sentence: Under Cascade §44-7241, Pacific Trust must pay or deny a complete claim within 30 days.

facts.name: 30-Day Claim Decision Rule
facts.sentence: The statutory payment period requires Pacific Trust to pay or deny a complete claim within 30 days.

facts.name: Statutory Claim Payment Timeline
facts.sentence: Cascade §44-7241 governs the statutory payment period for claims.

facts.name: Governing Law Jurisdiction
facts.sentence: The certificate is governed by the laws of the State of Cascade.

facts.name: Federal and State Law Jurisdiction
facts.sentence: Federal law applies to the certificate in addition to state law.

facts.name: ERISA Exemption Status
facts.sentence: This plan is exempt from ERISA.

facts.name: ERISA Exemption Reason
facts.sentence: The exemption from ERISA is due to the plan being classified as a governmental plan.

facts.name: Insurer Issuance Entity
facts.sentence: The insurer issuing the certificate is Pacific Trust Life & Annuity.

facts.name: Headquarters Location
facts.sentence: The headquarters or operational base of Pacific Trust Life & Annuity is located in Capital City, Cascade.

facts.name: Group Insurance Authority
facts.sentence: A Group Insurance Director holds authority over group insurance matters at Pacific Trust.

facts.name: Certificate Issuance Date
facts.sentence: The certificate was issued on January 1, 2024.
